what: ./judo.sh schema-upgrade fails with ProjectBuildingException because SCHEMA_DIR defaults to the model directory (project root), so the schema POM path is <root>/schema. Setting schema_dir=application makes it run, but no catalog page says schema_dir exists.
why: judo.sh derives SCHEMA_DIR from model_dir; in this layout the schema module lives under application/, and the catalog does not document schema_dir.
workaround: Ran schema_dir=application ./judo.sh schema-upgrade, and later the generate/execute route (see c07 F52 decision).

what: schema-upgrade runs apply (generate and execute in one step), so there is no moment to insert the hand-written backfill changeset that the catalog recommends. The catalog's schema-upgrade row does not warn about this.
why: The command table describes schema-upgrade as generate-and-apply; the backfill route needs generate, edit, then execute as separate steps.
workaround: Used judo-rdbms-schema:generate with the old model file, wrote 06_updateDataAfterIncremental by hand, then :execute.

what: F52 migration without a wipe: copy the pre-change RDBMS model and pg_dump first, generate the migration with the old model as base, hand-write the weight and returnWindowDays backfill in changeset 06, then execute. Products, settings and orders survived.
why: schema-upgrade cannot host the backfill, and the user asked for a documented route with no wipe.

what: Migration with data: weight (backfilled 500) and ShopConfig.returnWindowDays (backfilled 14) in migration 1, then a second migration adding stored soldUnits with an SQL backfill. Fixture test compares pre-migration products with the table.
why: Built per the user's F52 request.

what: Bulk price change: a Change prices row action on each category (instance operation with a percent input), one transaction, 2-decimal rounding, rejects 0, -100 or less, +1000 or more, changes list price only, hand-written audit rows, success snackbar.
why: Built per the F45 row.

what: Bulk price change is an instance row action on the category table, not a static collection operation.
why: Static collection operations on shared tables hit a generator bug seen in R11 (R11-7c).

what: Admin dashboard: DashboardInfo over the settings row with orders today, revenue today (cancelled excluded, shared price format), and top 5 best sellers by stored soldUnits with rowsPerPage 5.
why: Built per the F48 row.

what: Sorting by a derived aggregate gives a generated-SQL error (missing FROM-clause entry), and a nested filter or filter plus sort over the same type gives 'table name _iterator_N specified more than once' at runtime (HTTP 500 on the dashboard and on coupon creation).
why: Platform JQL-to-SQL generator bug for these expression shapes.
workaround: Made soldUnits a stored aggregate, maintained by checkout, cancel and return approval, and sorted on it with one selector.
proposed_target: JQL to SQL generator (sort over derived member, nested lambda over same type)

what: The top-N expression form is unclear: !sort(...)!heads(5) fails in asm2query with 'Missing variable name', and !heads(p | ..., 5) validates but returns only one row at runtime. The catalog lists !heads(n) without a working top-N example.
why: The catalog documents heads and sort separately; the lambda form and its runtime behaviour are not shown.
workaround: Used filter then sort with DESC and let the table page show 5 rows.

what: soldUnits is a STORED aggregate kept by checkout, cancel and return approval, instead of a derived sum, so the dashboard can sort it.
why: Derived aggregates cannot be sorted (see platform-bug on F48 SQL). The catalog recommends stored aggregates.

what: Returns: ReturnRequest owned by the order line (REQUESTED to APPROVED or REJECTED), window from delivery plus ShopConfig.returnWindowDays (default 14), approval restores stock and writes a history row with the refund, pages Return an item, My returns and Returns to review.
why: Built per the F49 row.

what: The Request return button exists only inside the window because a row action cannot be hidden per row (CLI rejects hiddenBy), so returnable lines get their own page.
why: The row action visibility property is not settable from the CLI (see cli-tool item on hiddenBy).
workaround: Separate Return an item page that lists only returnable lines; the operation re-checks the flag as its guard.

what: The CLI rejects hiddenBy and enabledBy on a TableOperation ('not defined for input object type TableOperationUpdateInput'), although tables-navigation.md lists both properties for ui:TableOperation.
why: The CLI input type does not match the documented property list.
workaround: Per-row hiding moved to a separate page (see decision on F49).

what: The label of a row action must be set on the operation form element (TableOperation::<op>::<op>), not on the TableOperation. Setting label on the TableOperation or on a guessed element name failed with 'element not found' or 'label not defined'.
why: Element naming and the label location for row actions are not shown in the catalog.
workaround: Set label on ...::changePricesTableOperation::changePrices and ...::requestReturnTableOperation::requestReturn.

what: The wishlist price came from a derived string (priceLabel = price plus ' EUR' in the model), so it was not localised and the generated numeric column showed a number without currency. The shared Price component cannot be placed on a generated table column.
why: No documented way to put the shared Price format on a generated table column; the model string hard-codes the currency.
workaround: Rebuilt the wishlist as a custom view page using Price (see the F41 built item).

what: The table column customizer hook key is imported by the generated tables but nothing consumes it, so a hook registered for a column never applies. The catalog's Custom Columns section presents it as working.
why: Grep over the generated frontend found no consumer of TABLE_COLUMN_CUSTOMIZER_HOOK_INTERFACE_KEY; the platform does not wire it.
workaround: Not used; wishlist moved to a custom component.

what: Setting DataColumn.customImplementation=true makes the generated table use useTrackService without importing it, so pnpm build fails with TS2304 in every such table. The builder also reports that TransferObjectTable.customImplementation is accepted by the CLI and does nothing.
why: Generator emits a call to a hook it does not import; the table-level flag has no effect in the generated code.
workaround: Reverted customImplementation on the columns, set it only on the table, then used a custom view page.
proposed_target: generator: DataColumn customImplementation emits useTrackService without import; TransferObjectTable.customImplementation no-op

what: Wishlist is a view page of a new TransferObjectType WishlistInfo (access Customer.myWishlist, 0..1) whose items element is a custom implementation, following the cart pattern. The generated wishlist access is kept for move and remove.
why: Column hooks and column customImplementation do not work (see the two platform-bug items).

what: Wishlist page uses the shared Price component ('12,00 EUR' in Hungarian), with loading, empty and error states, Move to cart and Remove through the generated service.
why: Round 12 UI fix for the wishlist price.

what: Notifications header: the bell navigates with clearNavigate so the breadcrumb reads Home, and AppBarExtras wraps the language switch and the bell in one flex row with no stray background.
why: Round 12 UI fixes requested by the user (Home breadcrumb, tidy header).

what: The notifications bell used navigate, which pushes the current page into the breadcrumb, so the page showed 'Home / Products' instead of 'Home'. The sidebar already used clearNavigate.
why: Builder picked the wrong navigation call; the breadcrumb practice page says useJudoNavigation offers clearNavigate for this.
workaround: Changed the bell to clearNavigate.

what: In the drawer, the generated layout stacks the AppBar extra components as a column, so the bell button stretched over the full drawer width and showed as a grey ellipse.
why: Generated layout of AppBar extra components has no documented row layout; the builder fixed it by wrapping them in one Box.
workaround: One flex Box wrapper inside AppBarExtras.

what: Shop branding (logo, title, primary colour) stays in the model. It is not read from the configuration singleton. A test checks logo and colour on five pages per app.
why: Theme colours are ActorType attributes and the logo and title are model elements, all applied at build time; editing palette.ts would need a .generator-ignore entry, which is forbidden.
workaround: Documented the decision and checked it in tests.

what: Builder claims there is no documented way to read brand values from a runtime settings row; palette and logo are fixed at start-up.
why: Builder's reading of theming.md, which says brand colours belong to model attributes; the catalog does not state whether runtime branding is possible.
workaround: Decision recorded (see F51 decision).

what: BusinessClock used the JVM zone (CET) while model Timestamp!now() uses the platform zone (UTC), so the return window was an hour off (a 0-day window stayed open). The catalog page on time zones says to use one clock for writing and comparing; the builder wrote the clock before reading it and claimed in R11 that both were UTC.
why: Builder did not consult the platform-behaviour page before writing the custom clock.
workaround: BusinessClock now uses the platform zone (JUDO_PLATFORM_DEFAULT_ZONE_ID, UTC by default); older rows keep the one-hour offset.

what: Timestamp!now() in model expressions follows the platform defaultZoneId (UTC here), while LocalDateTime.now() in custom Java follows the JVM zone; the builder confirmed this against the DB (deliveredAt 05:29 vs UTC 04:29).
why: Two clocks in one platform; the catalog states it and the builder verified it against data.

what: Admin product edits are audited by a post-call interceptor on the built-in update, one AuditEntry per changed field in the same transaction; the bulk price change writes its own rows through an AuditLog service.
why: Built-in update is intercepted and custom operations are not, as the catalog says.

what: Audit log: one row per changed product field (who, what, old and new value), read-only audit page; unchanged fields create no row; bulk price change rows appear too.
why: Built per the F50 row.

what: The builder could not find how to read old and new values in the update interceptor and decompiled the dispatcher jar with javap to learn UpdateInstanceCallPayload, without a kb search.
why: Interceptor payload access is not clear from the interceptor page as the builder read it (unverified); the kb was not searched first.
workaround: Used getInput() and getInstance() from the decompiled class.

what: Order lifecycle integration tests in a hand-written module application/order-tests: 8 tests (new to paid to shipped to delivered with history, refused steps change nothing, return once, stock back, cancel own orders). They found three bugs in ReturnService.
why: Built per the F53 row, in a module outside the generated test kit.
workaround: Hand-written module, see decision.

what: Use a hand-written module (application/order-tests) with the generated pom copied and its i18n-api version filled in, instead of the generated integration-test module.
why: The generated module cannot be read by Maven (empty i18n-api version), and the root fragment override did not win.
workaround: Removed the root fragment after one try; moved the sources to order-tests.

what: The generated application/integration-test/pom.xml declares hu.blackbelt.osgi.i18n:i18n-api with an empty version element, so Maven cannot read the project ('dependencies.dependency.version ... is missing').
why: Template or generator bug in the integration-test pom fragment; the empty element is not filled from a property.
workaround: Hand-written order-tests module with the version filled in.

what: The documented command 'mvn clean test -pl application/integration-test' fails from the project root with 'Could not find the selected project in the reactor', because the module is not in the root reactor. The osgi-ds page says the module is built standalone from its own directory.
why: Catalog command does not match the reactor layout described on the osgi page.
workaround: Ran mvn test from the module directory (later the order-tests module).

what: The testkit has no generated DAO module: the best-practices example uses a project AppDaoModules class that does not exist in the generated project, so the test failed with 'No implementation for ShopConfigDao was bound'. The builder wrote one @Provides per DAO.
why: Catalog example assumes a project DAO module; the generated project does not provide one and the page does not say how to make one.
workaround: Hand-written WebshopDaoModule over ReferenceInjector.

what: The new tests found the builder's own mistakes in ReturnService: an Optional passed to %f, an Optional in the history text, a getProductName call on the wrong object, and a guessed getCode method that is getErrorCode.
why: Builder wrote code against guessed generated APIs.
workaround: Fixed in ReturnService and the test.

what: One integration test failed with 'Outdated instance to update' (IllegalArgumentException in the update DAO processor) after the test changed the product's stock with a stale instance.
why: Probably an instance re-read is needed after an earlier update in the same test; not confirmed against the catalog.

what: Checkout E2E test (two products, address required, order shows cart total) in CI mode: playwright.ci.config.ts with retries and workers from the catalog, headless, waits on responses and on screen only. Passes with CI=true, no retry used.
why: Built per the F54 row.

what: The generated playwright.config.ts sets retries: 4 unconditionally (the template comment says retry on CI only). The catalog's troubleshooting page documents the fix as retries: process.env.CI ? 4 : 0.
why: Generator template ignores the CI condition; catalog already describes the fix.
workaround: Separate playwright.ci.config.ts and playwright.local.config.ts (not generated).

what: 'playwright install chromium' hangs during extraction on this machine, so the local config uses the installed Google Chrome channel.
why: Environment-specific install hang on the builder's machine.
workaround: playwright.local.config.ts with channel chrome and retries 0.

what: judo-cli query esm with --where fqn=... returns nothing, and --select dataType{name} or dataType.name is rejected (scalar fields only), so the builder decompiled and grepped generated code to learn names.
why: CLI query selection rules are not what the builder expected; the catalog page on the CLI was not consulted for query syntax first.
workaround: Used name filters and grep over generated sources.

what: fill creates a menu item for every new access, labelled with the type name (ReturnableItemInfo, ReturnInfo, WishlistInfo). A hand-made MenuItemAccess with a duplicate name fails validation silently or with NamedElementIsUniqueInItsContainer, and move --index did not change the drawer order.
why: Generator creates menu items from access names; CLI menu commands do not change generated order.
workaround: Deleted the extra menu item, relabelled the others, and used the documented menu customizer for order.

what: Menu order of both apps is set by the documented menu customizer hook (customer registerShellHooks MENU_ORDER, admin registerMenuOrder by title), not by model order.
why: Model creation order put Returns to review first and Dashboard last; the hook is the documented route.

what: Enumeration members have no label field (EnumerationMemberUpdateInput has only name, documentation, ordinal), so UI status text must come from a derived string member.
why: Platform input type for enumeration members; the builder read it from the GraphQL input type.
workaround: Derived statusLabel member on ReturnRequest mapped into the screens.

what: After every generate or build the target/judo-cli.jar is deleted, so judo.sh build -i failed with 'Unable to access jarfile' until generate-root was run. Same gap as S01 item 2 (recurring).
why: build-process says build downloads the jar; generate-root and generate delete it.
workaround: Ran ./judo.sh generate-root before each CLI call.

what: Each model change cost a stop, generate, build and start cycle of about 3 to 5 minutes (fixed sleeps of 125 to 150 seconds), and the full Playwright runs took about 8 minutes (admin) and 21 minutes (customer).
why: Full redeploy for each model edit and no hot reload used in this round.
workaround: Batched model edits before builds; ran full suites once at the end.

what: The generator writes only application_en-US.json; the Hungarian file is built by a project script (make-hu-translations.py) from the English keys, and new keys must be added to its dictionary each round. The catalog does not say how to keep a second locale file current.
why: Catalog i18n page covers switching, not maintaining a second generated-style locale file.
workaround: Project script scripts/make-hu-translations.py, run after each generate.

what: The test database is kept between runs, so tests broke on accumulated data: Wool socks ran out of stock (restocked by SQL), review, coupon and audit tables grew past one page, FK errors blocked category cleanup, and cleanup errors hid the real failure (a catch was added). F10 and F45 were flaky.
why: Round 12 is the first round that keeps data; earlier rounds wiped the DB and tests assumed an empty one.
workaround: Filter each test to its own stamp, show most rows, restock by SQL, catch cleanup errors; F10 flake fixed at the end.

what: Several Playwright assumptions were wrong: breadcrumb selected by role navigation (MUI breadcrumbs have none), a second Add-to-cart click was ignored while the first call was pending, the dashboard value was read before it loaded, and a price field showed '25.00 EUR' after blur instead of '25'.
why: Tests written against guessed DOM and timing; fixed by class selectors, waiting on responses, and checking the displayed format.
workaround: Changed selectors, awaited the POST response, asserted the displayed value.

what: Frontend build logs show 'XMI ID COLLISION DETECTED' errors for the admin and customer models, but the build still succeeded. The builder did not investigate them.
why: Generator reassigns the same XMI ids to Action objects; cause not checked.
proposed_target: generator: duplicate XMI ids for TabularReferenceField actions

what: kb_get on agent-docs/frontend/advanced-patterns.md returned 'not found', although kb_search had returned that same path.
why: Path mismatch between kb_search hit paths and kb_get lookup (unverified).
workaround: Read the file with grep and ctx_execute instead.

what: Only 18 of 365 tool calls in this chunk were kb calls. The kb guard warned about repeated source searching about 76 times, and the builder kept reading and grepping source. The orchestrator log later records 18 of 365 as well.
why: Standing rule (kb first for every question) was not followed in this round; the builder started with grep and reads.

what: Add-to-message snackbar for operation replies: a documented post-operation hook shows output.message in the snackbar and then calls onSubmit, instead of the generated second dialog.
why: Operations answer with a short ShopMessage; the generated flow opens a second dialog showing it.
